original_question: Can intermittent radio-mode AGN activity in cluster centres inject energy in a way that efficiently suppresses cooling flows throughout massive haloes, despite the facts that not every cluster shows central radio activity and that radiative cooling depends steeply on gas density, which makes stabilization difficult at all radii?
target_in_paper: the open problem of determining if and how the energy injected by intermittent “radio-mode” AGN feedback at cluster centres can efficiently suppress cooling flows across all radii of massive haloes
correct_elements: identifies the role of intermittent radio-mode AGN feedback at cluster centres; seeks to understand whether this energy injection can suppress cooling flows efficiently; notes that not every cluster shows central radio activity; acknowledges the steep density dependence of radiative cooling making stabilization difficult at all radii
missing_details: specify that this question arises in the context of semi-analytic models of galaxy formation aiming to match the bright end of the galaxy luminosity function
define “radio-mode” AGN feedback as episodic mechanical energy injection by jets or bubbles at the centres of cluster-mass dark matter haloes
quantify “cooling flows” as the radiative loss of thermal energy at rates Λ(T)∝ρ² and its impact on gas condensation in haloes
clarify the mass scale of the haloes considered (i.e. cluster-scale, M≳10¹⁴ M_⊙)
state the observational constraint that ensemble-averaged jet power appears sufficient to offset mean cooling rates [21]
mention the duty cycle or intermittency timescale of AGN radio activity relevant to the feedback process
specify the radial extent over which suppression is required (e.g. from the core out to r≈R_200)
refined_question: Within the framework of semi-analytic galaxy formation models developed to reproduce the observed bright end of the galaxy luminosity function, under what conditions and with what duty cycle can intermittent “radio-mode” AGN feedback—modeled as episodic mechanical energy injection by jets or bubbles at the centres of cluster-scale (M≳10¹⁴ M_⊙) dark matter haloes—inject sufficient power to offset radiative cooling (Λ(T)∝ρ²) and suppress cooling flows at all radii out to the virial radius, given that not every cluster exhibits central radio sources and that the steep density dependence of cooling makes stabilization challenging?
justification: The draft question closely mirrors the open problem posed in the paper’s discussion of AGN feedback (turn5view0, L132–L139), but omits the modeling context (semi-analytic techniques), explicit definitions of radio-mode feedback and cooling flows, the relevant halo mass scale, and the observational constraint on ensemble-averaged jet power [21]. The refined question incorporates these details to make it fully self-contained and faithful to the paper’s intent.
